newsitem.title: USA: Clinton "twisted his knee" -- White House.
newsitem.headline: Clinton "twisted his knee" -- White House.

text.p: President Bill Clinton was taken to hospital after twisting his knee early on Friday but was not seriously hurt, White House spokeswoman Mary Ellen Glynn said.
"He's fine, he wasn't sedated at all," Glynn said. "It looks like the president will not be playing golf today."
Clinton, 50, was to have returned to Washington late on Saturday, but would probably go back later on Friday, Glynn said.
Clinton slipped on some steps while walking between buildings at the Florida estate of Australian golfer Greg Norman in the middle of the night.
He hurt his right knee and was taken to St Mary's hospital in West Palm Beach. "He is resting comfortably, he was in some pain," Glynn said.
There had been no transfer of power to Vice-President Al Gore, as would happen if Clinton were rendered incapable of governing.
Clinton, 50, was to have returned to Washington late on Saturday, but would probably go back later on Friday, Glynn said.
Clinton was staying at Norman's estate, known as "Tranquility", in Hobe Sound, Florida, and had stayed up late chatting with the golfer.
He was in Florida to take part in a two-day golf tournament hosted by Norman, beginning on Friday. On Thursday night he had addressed a political fund-raising dinner there.

Clinton was reelected to a second four-year term last November. He is due to meet Russian President Boris Yeltsin in Helsinki next week for talks on NATO expansion into eastern Europe and other matters.
